decision.policy: Typst is the default PDF path; LuaLaTeX remains a supported compatibility and diagnostic backend.
review_triggers: a publisher or printer requires a backend-specific source or PDF feature
PDF/UA evaluation materially changes the accessibility comparison
a required technical-book feature fails in the default backend
a pinned toolchain upgrade changes reliability or output fidelity

measurement.method: One sequential primary 7 x 10 render per backend with network disabled and ephemeral container caches.

criteria.label: Required-feature fidelity
criteria.rationale: Both preserve the shared specimen contract; Typst also has the evaluated sidenote profile while LuaLaTeX currently uses the semantic footnote fallback.

criteria.label: Typography and page control
criteria.rationale: Both pass trim, containment, recto, blank-page, font, and pagination checks; LuaLaTeX retains the deeper mature page-composition system.

criteria.label: Reliability and diagnostics
criteria.rationale: Both build reproducibly, but Typst currently emits the known typst-gather glibc fallback warning while LuaLaTeX completes without a captured warning.

criteria.label: Template maintainability
criteria.rationale: Typst keeps the primary adapter in one modern source file and consumes SVG directly; LuaLaTeX requires several TeX partials, package knowledge, and staged PDF-vector assets.

criteria.label: Accessibility and PDF standards
criteria.rationale: Typst emits a tagged PDF and LuaLaTeX does not, but neither output has passed the later PDF/UA structure and assistive-technology evaluation.

criteria.label: Build speed
criteria.rationale: On the recorded sequential run Typst took 8.07 seconds and LuaLaTeX took 24.10 seconds for the same primary specimen.

criteria.label: Ecosystem fit for circuits, chemistry, and math
criteria.rationale: Portable generators cover selected workflows equally, while the mature TeX ecosystem remains broader for specialized mathematical and scientific publishing.

criteria.label: Long-term portability
criteria.rationale: Both are pinned and open source; TeX has the longer archival history and broader publisher tooling, while Typst and its Quarto integration are still evolving.
